mainTopic: The reasons for the joy of ט״ו באב, the vineyard dances described in the משנה, and the future dance of the צדיקים that closes מסכת תענית
overview: The גמרא finishes its list of reasons why ט״ו באב was a day of joy. The roadblocks to ירושלים were removed. The dead of ביתר were finally buried, and in יבנה the ברכה of הטוב והמטיב was set up because of it. Wood-cutting for the מערכה on the מזבח ended, since the sun is too weak to dry the wood after that date, and people called the day 'the day the sickle breaks.' From then on, whoever adds gains life, and whoever does not add is 'gathered,' meaning his mother will bury him. Next the גמרא explains the rest of the משנה. Everyone, even the king's daughter, borrowed white clothes so that no poor girl would be shamed, and the clothes needed טבילה even if they had been stored in a box. Unmarried men went to the vineyards to find a wife, and each group of girls called out its own strength. The מסכת ends with רבי אלעזר's promise of a future dance of the צדיקים, where each one will point to ה׳ and say 'This is our God,' followed by the הדרן.

steps.title: End of the earlier reason: people may go up wherever they wish
steps.stepSummary: The text finishes the previous reason for ט״ו באב: the guards on the roads were removed, so people could go up to any place they wanted.
steps.simpleTranslation: …they may go up to wherever they wish.
steps.whatsHappening: This is just the last words of a reason the גמרא was already explaining before this section begins. The guards blocking the roads were removed, and people were now free to travel where they wanted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, guards had been placed on the roads to stop people from going up to ירושלים. On ט״ו באב they were removed, and the king said people could go wherever they chose. That freedom is one reason the day was a celebration.

keyTerms.meaning: They may go up (travel up to a holy place)

phrases.english: to whichever they wish, they may go up.
phrases.notes: This is the end of a sentence that started before this section, about the guards being taken off the roads.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the earlier reason for ט״ו באב given before this section begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The roadblocks were removed, so people were free to go up wherever they wished.

steps.title: רב מתנה: the dead of ביתר were buried on this day
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה gives a new reason for the joy of ט״ו באב: it was the day the people killed at ביתר were finally allowed to be buried.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה said: It was the day the slain of ביתר were given over for burial.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנה offers another reason why ט״ו באב was a happy day. On that day the bodies of the people killed at ביתר were finally released for burial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a separate reason from the earlier ones. The joy is about the dignity of the dead: the bodies were finally allowed to be buried.

keyTerms.meaning: Were given over (allowed) to be buried

phrases.english: Rav Mattana said:
It is the day the slain of Beitar were given over for burial.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new, separate reason for the joy of ט״ו באב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ט״ו באב is a day of joy because the dead of ביתר were allowed burial on it.

steps.title: The ברכה of הטוב והמטיב was set up in יבנה because of ביתר
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה adds that on that same day the חכמים in יבנה set up the ברכה 'הטוב והמטיב.' Each half of the ברכה thanks ה׳ for something different.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב מתנה said: On that same day the slain of ביתר were given for burial, they set up in יבנה the ברכה 'Who is good and does good.' 'Who is good' because the bodies did not rot. 'And does good' because they were given over for burial.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנה brings a second, related statement: the ברכה of הטוב והמטיב was set up because of this event. He explains what each word of the ברכה is thanking ה׳ for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There were two separate kindnesses, so the ברכה has two parts. 'הטוב' thanks ה׳ that the bodies stayed whole and did not rot while they waited. 'המטיב' thanks ה׳ that they were finally buried.

keyTerms.meaning: They set up (made an official rule)
The town where the חכמים gathered after the חורבן
'Who is good and does good,' a ברכה

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains where the ברכה of הטוב והמטיב came from. It is a ברכה we still say today.

phrases.english: And Rav Mattana said:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹתוֹ יוֹם שֶׁנִּתְּנוּ הֲרוּגֵי בֵיתֵּר לִקְבוּרָה,
phrases.english: That same day the slain of Beitar were given over for burial,
they instituted in Yavne 'Who is good and does good':
'Who is good': that they did not rot,
phrases.notes: The bodies lay unburied for a long time but stayed whole. That was a kindness all by itself.

phrases.english: 'and does good': that they were given over for burial.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second statement by the same רב מתנה, building on the event he just mentioned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברכה הטוב והמטיב was set up in יבנה. 'הטוב' is for the bodies not rotting, and 'המטיב' is for their burial.

steps.title: רבה and רב יוסף: the day they stopped cutting wood for the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף give another reason: ט״ו באב was the day they stopped cutting wood for the fire on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף both said: It is the day they stopped cutting wood for the מערכה.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים together give another reason for the celebration. On ט״ו באב the yearly job of cutting wood for the מזבח was finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reason has to do with the work for the בית המקדש, not with national history. Finishing an important yearly מצוה was a cause for joy. The proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The pile of wood burning on the מזבח

phrases.english: Rabba and Rav Yosef, who both say:
It is the day they stopped cutting wood for the arrangement on the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds yet another separate reason for the joy of ט״ו באב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ט״ו באב is a day of joy because the wood-cutting for the מערכה ended on it.

steps.title: Proof from רבי אליעזר הגדול: the sun is too weak to dry the wood
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רבה and רב יוסף. From ט״ו באב on, the sun gets weaker, so newly cut wood would not dry properly. That is why they stopped cutting.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי אליעזר הגדול says: From ט״ו באב onward the strength of the sun weakens, and they would not cut wood for the מערכה, because it would not dry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that ט״ו באב really was the last day for cutting wood. It also gives the reason why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא explains why the date matters. After ט״ו באב the sun is weaker, so freshly cut wood stays damp. Damp wood was not good for the מזבח, so cutting stopped on that day.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Eliezer the Great says:
From the fifteenth of Av onward
the strength of the sun grows weak,
and they would not cut wood for the arrangement,
because they are not dry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the statement of רבה and רב יוסף with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That ט״ו באב was the day wood-cutting for the מערכה stopped.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי אליעזר הגדול: after ט״ו באב the sun is too weak to dry the wood.

steps.title: רב מנשיא: they called it 'the day the sickle breaks'
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשיא adds that people had a nickname for ט״ו באב: 'the day of breaking the sickle,' because the wood-cutting was over.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מנשיא said: And they called it 'the day of the breaking of the sickle.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב מנשיא adds a detail to the wood-cutting reason. The day was known by a popular name, which showed that the cutting tools were put away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The nickname backs up the idea that ט״ו באב marked the end of cutting wood. The tool is 'broken' because it is no longer needed for the rest of the year.

phrases.english: Rav Menashya said:
And they called it the day of the breaking of the sickle.
phrases.notes: A מגל is a cutting tool. It is 'broken' in the sense that it gets put away, since no more wood is cut.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a popular name for the day that fits the wood-cutting reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ט״ו באב was called 'יום תבר מגל' because wood-cutting stopped.

steps.title: From now on: whoever adds will add, and whoever does not will be gathered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a warning. From ט״ו באב on, a person who adds will gain more life, and a person who does not add will be 'gathered.'
steps.simpleTranslation: From here onward, whoever adds will have more added to him, and whoever does not add will be gathered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a short saying for the time after ט״ו באב. It uses a wordplay to say that a person should add something from this point on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The saying plays on similar-sounding words: מוסיף/יוסיף (add) and יאסף (be gathered). The words 'from here onward' connect it to ט״ו באב, when the nights start getting longer. What 'gathered' means is explained in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Will have more added (to his life)

phrases.english: From here onward,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means ט״ו באב, the day we have been discussing.

phrases.english: one who adds will have added to him,
phrases.notes: The line doesn't say what to add. The usual understanding is more Torah learning at night, since the nights are getting longer.

phrases.english: and one who does not add will be gathered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the turning point of ט״ו באב, when the days get shorter, to teach a lesson.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From ט״ו באב on, one who adds gains life, and one who does not add is 'gathered.'

steps.title: What does 'he will be gathered' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word יאסף means in the saying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what the unclear word 'יאסף' means. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Gathered' could mean several things, so the גמרא wants an exact meaning. This is a real question, not an attack on the saying.

phrases.english: What is 'he will be gathered'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a word in the saying just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word יאסף in the saying.

steps.title: רב יוסף: his mother will bury him
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that 'gathered' means the person will die young, so early that his own mother will bury him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: His mother will bury him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question. 'Gathered' means dying young, before one's own mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Gathered' is a word for being brought to the grave. Saying his mother will bury him shows how early the death would be. This makes the saying a serious warning: adding brings life, and not adding cuts life short.
steps.whatToRemember: ט״ו באב has many reasons for joy. The roadblocks were removed, the dead of ביתר were buried (the source of הטוב והמטיב), and wood-cutting for the מערכה ended (יום תבר מגל). From ט״ו באב on, whoever adds gains life, and whoever does not is 'gathered,' meaning his mother will bury him.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
His mother will bury him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the meaning of יאסף.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יאסף means he will die young, so young that his mother will bury him.

steps.title: Everyone borrows white clothes so no one is embarrassed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the daughters of ירושלים going out, and brings a ברייתא: each girl borrowed white clothes from a girl of slightly lower rank, and all of ישראל borrowed from each other, so that a girl without her own clothes would not be embarrassed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'On which the daughters of ירושלים...' The Rabbis taught: The king's daughter borrows from the daughter of the כהן גדול. The daughter of the כהן גדול borrows from the daughter of the סגן. The daughter of the סגן borrows from the daughter of the משוח מלחמה. The daughter of the משוח מלחמה borrows from the daughter of a regular כהן. And all of ישראל borrow from each other, so as not to embarrass someone who has none.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes the line about the daughters of ירושלים going out in borrowed white clothes. It then brings a ברייתא that explains who borrowed from whom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already said the girls went out in borrowed white clothes 'so as not to embarrass one who has none.' The ברייתא adds who borrowed from whom: even the king's daughter borrows, all the way down the line. If everyone wears borrowed clothes, no girl can be picked out as poor.

keyTerms.meaning: The deputy of the כהן גדול
The כהן anointed to speak to the army before battle

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a whole community arranging its celebration so that the poorest person will not feel ashamed.

phrases.english: On which the daughters of Jerusalem, etc.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה again: on ט״ו באב and יום הכיפורים the girls went out in borrowed white clothes.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: בַּת מֶלֶךְ שׁוֹאֶלֶת מִבַּת כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל,
phrases.english: The king's daughter borrows from the High Priest's daughter,
phrases.notes: She borrows white clothes. The text doesn't say it, but that's what the משנה was talking about.

phrases.english: the High Priest's daughter, from the deputy High Priest's daughter,
and the deputy's daughter, from the daughter of the priest anointed for war,

phrases.aramaic: וּבַת מְשׁוּחַ מִלְחָמָה — מִבַּת כֹּהֵן הֶדְיוֹט,
phrases.english: and the daughter of the priest anointed for war, from a regular priest's daughter,
and all of Israel borrow from one another

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא (יִתְבַּיֵּישׁ) [לְבַיֵּישׁ] אֶת מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ.
phrases.english: so as not to embarrass the one who has none.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets, 'to embarrass,' is the corrected wording.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁבָּהֶן בְּנוֹת יְרוּשָׁלַיִם כּוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the list of reasons for the joy of ט״ו באב (steps 1-9), the גמרא moves on to explain the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone, from the king's daughter down, borrowed white clothes so that a girl without her own would not be shamed.

steps.title: Even clothes stored away in a box need immersion
steps.stepSummary: The משנה said all the borrowed clothes needed טבילה. רבי אלעזר adds that this applies even to clothes that were folded and put away in a box.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: All the clothes need טבילה. רבי אלעזר said: Even if they were folded and lying in a box.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, that all the borrowed clothes needed טבילה. רבי אלעזר adds how far this rule goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think clothes folded away in a box were not touched and are surely טהור. רבי אלעזר says they still need טבילה. The rule covers every borrowed garment with no exceptions.

keyTerms.meaning: Items; here it means the clothes

steps.confusionAlert: כלים usually means utensils or vessels, but here it means the borrowed white clothes.

phrases.english: All the garments require immersion.
Rabbi Elazar said:
Even if they are folded and lying in a box.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַכֵּלִים טְעוּנִין טְבִילָה. אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the משנה line by line.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The borrowed clothes need טבילה even if they were stored folded in a box.

steps.title: Men without wives went to the vineyards
steps.stepSummary: The משנה said the girls went out and danced in the vineyards. A תנא explains that a man without a wife would go there to find one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: The daughters of ישראל would go out and dance in the vineyards. A תנא taught: A man who has no wife would turn to there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the girls dancing in the vineyards, and a תנא explains why men came there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only described the girls dancing. The תנא tells us what the dancing was for: it was a time for unmarried men to find a wife.

phrases.english: The daughters of Israel go out and dance in the vineyards.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא: מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אִשָּׁה, נִפְנֶה לְשָׁם.
phrases.english: It was taught: One who has no wife would turn to there.
phrases.notes: He means he would go to the vineyards to find a wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּנוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל יוֹצְאוֹת וְחוֹלוֹת בַּכְּרָמִים. תָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unmarried men went to the vineyards on these days to find a wife.

steps.title: What each group of girls called out
steps.stepSummary: The משנה quoted only what the well-born girls said. A ברייתא gives three calls: the beautiful girls praised beauty, the well-born girls praised family, and the plain girls asked to be married for the sake of Heaven and adorned with gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: The well-born among them would say, 'Young man...' The Rabbis taught: What would the beautiful ones say? 'Look at beauty, because a wife is only for beauty.' What would the well-born ones say? 'Look at family, because a wife is only for children.' What would the plain ones say? 'Make your choice for the sake of Heaven, as long as you adorn us with gold.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה about what the well-born girls said, then brings a ברייתא that gives what each kind of girl called out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא adds two more groups to the one in the משנה. Each group points to its own strength: beauty, good family for the children, or doing a מצוה for the sake of Heaven. The plain girls add that if the man adorns them with gold after the wedding, they will look beautiful too.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא finished explaining the משנה: everyone borrowed white clothes to protect the poor, the clothes needed טבילה, and the vineyard dance was a time for men to find a wife, with each group of girls calling out its own strength.

phrases.aramaic: מְיוּחָסוֹת שֶׁבָּהֶן הָיוּ אוֹמְרוֹת: בָּחוּר וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: The well-born among them would say: Young man, etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה, which goes on: 'lift up your eyes and see what you choose.'

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
What would the beautiful ones among them say?
Set your eyes on beauty,
for a wife is only for beauty.
What would the well-born ones among them say?
Set your eyes on family,
because a wife is only for children.
What would the plain ones among them say?
Take your purchase for the sake of Heaven,
as long as you adorn us with gold.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְיוּחָסוֹת שֶׁבָּהֶן הָיוּ אוֹמְרוֹת: בָּחוּר וְכוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the vineyard scene from step 12 by giving what the girls said.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Beautiful girls pointed to beauty, well-born girls pointed to family and children, and plain girls asked to be chosen for the sake of Heaven and adorned with gold.

steps.title: The future dance of the צדיקים in גן עדן
steps.stepSummary: עולא ביראה quotes רבי אלעזר: in the future, הקדוש ברוך הוא will arrange a dance for the צדיקים in גן עדן and sit among them. Each one will point to Him with his finger, as the פסוק in ישעיהו says, 'Behold, this is our God.'
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא from בירא said in the name of רבי אלעזר: In the future, הקדוש ברוך הוא will make a dance circle for the righteous. He will sit among them in גן עדן, and each one of them will point with his finger. As the פסוק says: 'And it will be said on that day: Behold, this is our God, for whom we waited, that He might save us. This is ה׳, for whom we waited. We will be glad and rejoice in His salvation.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the מסכת with a hopeful statement about a future dance of the צדיקים, tied to the dancing in the vineyards it just discussed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source is the word 'זה' (this) in the פסוק, which is said twice. You only say 'this' about something you can point at. So רבי אלעזר learns that in the future God will be so clearly revealed that each צדיק can point and say 'This is our God.'

keyTerms.meaning: A dance, often a circle dance
The Garden of Eden, where the righteous are rewarded
We hoped for Him, we waited for Him

steps.whatToRemember: The מסכת that deals with fasts and troubles ends with joy: a future dance where God is so clearly revealed that every צדיק can point to Him and say 'This is our God.'
steps.whyThisMatters: It is a tradition to end a מסכת on a hopeful note. Here the dancing of the girls on ט״ו באב and יום כיפור leads into the greatest dance of all, in the days to come.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר עוּלָּא בִּירָאָה, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Ulla of Bira'a said that Rabbi Elazar said:
In the future, the Holy One, Blessed be He,
will make a dance for the righteous,
and He will sit among them in the Garden of Eden,
and each and every one will point with his finger,
as it is stated: "And it will be said on that day:

phrases.aramaic: הִנֵּה אֱלֹהֵינוּ זֶה קִוִּינוּ לוֹ וְיוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ
phrases.english: Behold, this is our God, for whom we waited, that He might save us.
This is the Lord, for whom we waited;
we will be glad and rejoice in His salvation."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא בִּירָאָה, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the theme of dancing from the vineyard dances (Step 12). It moves from the girls' dance in this world to the צדיקים' dance in the future.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the future God will lead a dance of the צדיקים in גן עדן, and His presence will be so clear that each one can point and say 'This is our God' (learned from 'זה' in ישעיהו 25:9).

steps.title: הדרן — Closing the פרק בשלשה פרקים and מסכת תענית
steps.stepSummary: The traditional הדרן formula closes the fourth פרק, called 'בשלשה פרקים', and announces that מסכת תענית is finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, 'בשלשה פרקים', and מסכת תענית is concluded.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not part of the discussion. It is the formal closing line that ends the פרק and the whole מסכת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'הדרן עלך' means 'we will return to you.' It expresses the learner's promise to come back and review. Because this is the last פרק, it adds that the whole מסכת תענית is now complete.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you, the closing formula at the end of a chapter

steps.whatToRemember: מסכת תענית is complete. The הדרן is a promise to keep coming back to what we learned.

phrases.english: We will return to you, "In three times"
phrases.notes: 'בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה פְּרָקִים' is the name of this פרק, taken from its opening words.

phrases.english: and Tractate Taanit is concluded.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַרַן עֲלָךְ בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה פְּרָקִים וּסְלִיקָא לַהּ מַסֶּכֶת תַּעֲנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally closes the פרק and the מסכת after the final aggadic statement.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The fourth פרק, בשלשה פרקים, and all of מסכת תענית are complete, with a commitment to return and review.
